Events.RelatedBody: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Aspire. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Aspire Dashboard's unauthenticated NotFound route can permit telemetry deletion in both standalone and AppHost-hosted deployments. In standalone deployments using browser-token authentication, it can also expose the browser token. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22148 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Critical - **Score:** 9.1 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N` - **Weakness:** CWE-862 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire Dashboard Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- Aspire Dashboard | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 Both 13.6.3 and 13.6.4 contain the unauthenticated NotFound route. ### Aspire Dashboard SDK packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-musl-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-musl-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Aspire Dashboard releases through 13.6.4 are affected, whether deployed independently or launched by an Aspire AppHost. For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, check the resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk package versions against the affected ranges above. If the AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, check the version of that Dashboard instead. Aspire ships independently of .NET; installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not replace the Dashboard. ### How do I fix the issue? Update Aspire Dashboard to version 13.6.5 or later. Neither 13.6.3 nor 13.6.4 is a fixed upgrade target. For container deployments, explicitly set the Dashboard image to `mcr.microsoft.com/aspire/dashboard:13.6.5` and recreate or redeploy the container. Replace older version tags and nightly image references, including those in generated Docker Compose or Kubernetes manifests, with this fixed stable image. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace an image reference in an existing deployment manifest. For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, update any explicit Aspire.Hosting.AppHost version, including a central package version, to 13.6.5 or later. If that reference is supplied implicitly by Aspire.AppHost.Sdk, update the SDK reference to 13.6.5 or later instead. Restore and rebuild the AppHost, verify that its resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk packages are 13.6.5 or later, and restart the AppHost to run the updated Dashboard. If your AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, update the Dashboard in that selected bundle or location to 13.6.5 or later and restart the AppHost. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace that Dashboard. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue in the Aspire repository at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-118740](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-118740) ### Acknowledgements - Weeraphat Srisutham ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. ASP.NET Core Identity scaffolding templates use the request-supplied email instead of the account's stored email for password-reset and confirmation messages. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/Scaffolding/issues/3959 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.1 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-640 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages Updating scaffolding packages/tools does not repair previously generated application code. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc contains the affected templates. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design is a parent package that brings in the MVC generator through a minimum-version dependency. For Design, applicability depends on the resolved MVC generator: a project that independently resolves a fixed MVC version does not become vulnerable merely because it retains an older Design reference. ### 8.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.23 | 8.0.24 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.23 | 8.0.24 ### 9.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.12 | 9.0.13 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.12 | 9.0.13 ### 10.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.2 | 10.0.3 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.2 | 10.0.3 ### Additional known affected scaffolding prereleases These are exact known affected versions, not continuous prerelease intervals. Version 20.3.0 supports .NET 8, 9, 10 and 11. Install it as a .NET tool, not as a project package reference. The MVC and Design project packages use the separate fixed versions listed above; 20.3.0 is not a version of those packages. ### Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.x Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold) | >= 20.0.0-preview.1.26156.3, <= 20.1.0 | 20.3.0 The 20.x tool contains the vulnerable Identity and Blazor templates for .NET 8.0 through 11.0. ### Affected legacy prereleases The following exact versions also contain affected templates: - [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) and [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design): `11.0.0-preview.1.26156.3` and `11.0.0-preview.1.26230.3`. - [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet): `10.0.0-rc.1.25458.5` and `10.0.0-rc.1.25468.1`. Apply the generated-code repair below to applications created with these versions. For new scaffolding, use the Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.3.0 tool, which supports .NET 8 through 11. Migrating to that tool is not an update to an MVC or Design project package reference and does not repair previously generated code. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Check both the installed scaffolding package/tool version and the code it generated. Applications generated with an affected template remain affected after the tool is updated unless their handlers are corrected. The `dotnet-aspnet-codegenerator` command loads generators from the application's dependencies. Check the project's Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design and Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc references against the versions above; updating only the command-line tool does not replace those project dependencies. For applications created with `dotnet new`, check the selected SDK with `dotnet --version` in the working directory. Use `dotnet new list` to identify available templates and `dotnet new uninstall` without arguments to list separately installed template packages. Keep `Input.Email` for the account lookup; do not use it as the message recipient. Apply the change to both handlers, including their Blazor equivalents, then rebuild and redeploy. **Version Used**: .NET 11.0.100 SDK, C# 15

**Steps to Reproduce**:

1. Save the following two files in an empty folder.

`.editorconfig`
```ini
root = true

[*.cs]
dotnet_diagnostic.IDE0072.severity = warning
```

`repro.cs`
```csharp
#:property TargetFramework=net11.0
#:property EnforceCodeStyleInBuild=true

public closed class Shape;
public sealed class Circle : Shape;
public sealed class Square : Shape;

public static class Describer
{
    public static string Describe(Shape shape) =>
        shape switch
        {
            Circle => "circle",
            Square => "square",
        };
}
```

2. Run `dotnet build repro.cs`.

**Diagnostic Id**: `IDE0072: Populate switch`

**Expected Behavior**: No diagnostic. Every direct descendant of the closed class is handled, so the compiler treats the switch as exhaustive. It reports no CS8509, and removing the `Square` arm does produce CS8509.

**Actual Behavior**:

```
repro.cs(16,15): warning IDE0072: Populate switch
```

IDE0072 appears to only recognise enums, so it doesn't know a closed hierarchy is complete. It should either skip switches over closed hierarchies, or recognise them and only report when a descendant is actually missing. The same may apply to switches over union types.

Events.RelatedBody:
### Describe the bug

A parallel solution-level pack encountered an intermittent compiler file-lock error:

```text
Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Remote.Razor net10.0 win-arm64 failed with 1 error(s)
CSC : error CS2012: Cannot open 'D:\R2\artifacts\obj\Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Remote.Razor\Release\net10.0\win-arm64\Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Remote.Razor.dll' for writing -- The process cannot access the file ... because it is being used by another process.
```

This was observed on Windows in a checkout of `tmat/roslyn` branch `fix-pack` at commit tmat/roslyn@85abc837dcd24928be4c2f00df8ce7539225f6c9. That branch contains a packaging workaround in `eng/targets/Imports.targets` not present in the parent revision. It has not been established whether the error also reproduces on current `main` without that workaround.

### Reproduction

Run a parallel solution-level pack, e.g. `dotnet pack -mt`. The failure appears timing-dependent; a reliable standalone reproduction and a binlog of the failing run are not yet available.

### Evidence and suspected cause

A separate **successful** `dotnet pack -mt --no-restore` binlog on the same checkout shows two evaluations of `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Remote.Razor.csproj` for `Release`, `net10.0`, `win-arm64` with the same intermediate output directory as the error above. Their global property sets differ only in `SelfContained`: one has the global property `SelfContained=false`, and the other does not have it. MSBuild treats those as distinct project instances even though their intermediate paths coincide.

Potential paths into this project include:

- [The thin client's `PublishBundledLanguageServer` target](https://github.com/tmat/roslyn/blob/85abc837dcd24928be4c2f00df8ce7539225f6c9/src/LanguageServer/roslyn-language-server/roslyn-language-server.csproj#L60-L63) explicitly passes `SelfContained=$(SelfContained)` when publishing the language server; the language server references the VS Code Razor extension, which references Remote.Razor.
- [The ARM64 CoreComponents VSIX reference](https://github.com/tmat/roslyn/blob/85abc837dcd24928be4c2f00df8ce7539225f6c9/src/Razor/src/Razor/src/Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Remote.Razor.CoreComponents/CoreComponents.props#L34-L43) requests `PublishProjectOutputGroup` with the matching TFM/RID, but does not explicitly set `SelfContained`. [That output group depends on `Publish`](https://github.com/tmat/roslyn/blob/85abc837dcd24928be4c2f00df8ce7539225f6c9/src/Razor/src/Razor/src/Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Remote.Razor/Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Remote.Razor.csproj#L99).

These paths are candidates; the successful log establishes the property/output-path collision, but does **not** prove which process held the file or that the two instances compiled concurrently during the failed run. An unrelated process holding the file is also possible. A failing binlog and/or file-handle trace would confirm the actual writer.

If concurrent project instances are responsible, the build should normalize the relevant **global** properties at the call boundaries, or use distinct intermediate paths for configurations that need separate instances.

### Describe the bug

[CA2026](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/fundamentals/code-analysis/quality-rules/ca2026) raises a warning when using JsonDocument.Parse(...).RootElement and suggests using JsonElement.Parse(...) instead.  The autofix for this generates non-compiling code.  

### Steps to reproduce

Write code that uses the incorrect pattern.

```lang=C#
var root = JsonDocument.Parse(response).RootElement;
```

Run the auto-fix.  The below is the result, which does not compile:

```lang=C#
var root = JsonElement.Parse(response, JsonDocument.Parse(response));
```

### Expected behavior

The autofix should not place in an invented value for the JsonDocumentOptions optional value.  It should leave that blank, or conceivably include an options value if one is already present in the file.

Below is what I would expect to see from the autofix.

```lang=C#
var root = JsonElement.Parse(response);
```

### Actual behavior

The below is the result, which does not compile:

```lang=C#
var root = JsonElement.Parse(response, JsonDocument.Parse(response));
```

### Is this a regression?

_No response_

_No response_

Issues.Title: [release/3.1] Reset current_no_gc_region_info after leaving no gc region implicitly
Issues.Body:
Backport https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/73602.

## Customer Impact
Customers reported occasional `System.InvalidOperationException` with message `The NoGCRegion mode was already in progress` when calling `GC.TryStartNoGCRegion`. This is preventing them from using this optimization and impacting their cold start latencies.

## Testing
Customers have tried the fix on .NET 6 overnight and reported the exception never appears again. Meanwhile, there is an unpatched machine and observed 72 exceptions of the same type in the same time interval, proving this does fix the bug.

## Risk
Low. This only impact customer using `TryStartNoGCRegion`, and this is the right thing to do.

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Assembly version for DispatchProxy shim is too low resulting in duplicate types for DispatchProxy
Issues.Body:
Create a new `netstandard2.1` library.
Add a reference to `<PackageReference Include="System.Reflection.DispatchProxy" Version="4.7.1" />`
Try to use `DispatchProxy`

Expected: 
`DispatchProxy` is resolved from `netstandard.dll`

Actual:
```
error CS0433: The type 'DispatchProxy' exists in both 'System.Reflection.DispatchProxy, Version=4.0.6.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b03f5f7f11d50a3a' and 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51'
```


Build contains conflict message:
```
Encountered conflict between 'CopyLocal:C:\src\dotnet\runtime\artifacts\bin\testPackages\cache\system.reflection.dispatchproxy\4.7.1\lib\netstandard2.0\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll' and 'Runtime:C:\Program Files\dotnet\packs\NETStandard.Library.Ref\2.1.0\ref\netstandard2.1\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll'. Choosing 'CopyLocal:C:\src\dotnet\runtime\artifacts\bin\testPackages\cache\system.reflection.dispatchproxy\4.7.1\lib\netstandard2.0\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll' because AssemblyVersion '4.0.6.0' is greater than '4.0.5.0'.
```

Other shims avoid this by setting the AssemblyVersion higher than that which was previously shipped.

Issues.Title: Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs
Issues.Body:
I'm completely perplexed.

I created a .Net Standard 2.0 library project.

I explicity added an AssemblyInfo.cs file, we need this because we use this utility to "stamp" our assemblies when we build them:

https://github.com/ygoe/NetRevisionTool

That utility is run as a pre/post build event and temporarily replaces placeholders in the AssemblyInformationalVersion attribute with runtime values (like repo folder name, commit ID, branch etc etc).

The completed assembly then has this info "burned" into it as we go forward.

.Net Standard is not working with this.

1. It seems to populatethe Package Version (in the project's Package section) with whatever we put into AssemblyInfo.cs for AssemblyInformationalVersion.
2. The version of the generated nuget package is always set as 1.0.0.

This is just mind blowing, is there no way we can do this seemingly simple operation any more if adopt .Net Standard?
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs " (#1775)

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions" (#1777)

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1" (#1787)

Issues.Title: Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions" (#1786)

Issues.Title: linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem
Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem" (#1792)

Issues.Title: Strong name signature not valid
Issues.Body:
Since I've ported a ClickOnce application from .NET Framework 4.6.1 to .NET Standard 2.0, the message _"Strong assembly name signature not valid for **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**"_ appears when trying to install or update the application. So the next step was to verify the assembly strong name by using the [Strong Name Tool](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/tools/sn-exe-strong-name-tool) to make sure, that everything is fine, but:

```sh
> sn.exe -v Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll

Microsoft (R) .NET Framework Strong Name Utility Version 4.0.30319.0
Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved.

Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll is a delay-signed or test-signed assembly
```

Additional information:

- The assembly versions `161.46041.41` and `161.46367.54` ended up in the same result
- This issue looks very similar to [this](https://www.damirscorner.com/blog/posts/20140502-StrongNameValidationFailedSecurityException.html)
- @markingmyname / @olprod: The root package, which is required for [Server Management Objects (SMOs)](https://docs.microsoft.com/sql/relational-databases/server-management-objects-smo/overview-smo?view=sql-server-ver15), is:
  - [Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects)
    - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment
      - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Authoring
        - **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**
- This issue appears on windows server machines but the software runs on different machines and I would like to avoid temporary workarounds such as editing the registry and activate the strong name bypass feature because of the forced validation on windows server machines
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Strong name signature not valid" (#1789)

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Best Regards, Raphael --- ### Original Comments #### Raphael Affolter on 1/20/2020, 04:03 AM:

I forgot to mention: .Net Framework 4.6.1

#### Feedback Bot on 1/20/2020, 06:51 PM:

We have directed your feedback to the appropriate engineering team for further evaluation. The team will review the feedback and notify you about the next steps.

#### Raphael Affolter on 2/7/2020, 08:39 AM:

Because we print a lot, we really suffer from this performance penalty.

Also reading PaperSizes and PaperSources from the printer settings is slow caused by the same problem.

Could you please inform me about a possible fix?

Best Regards,

Raphael

#### Raphael Affolter on 2/7/2020, 10:33 AM:

In my opinion the fix is easy: replace GetOutputPort by OutputPort in the call to

FastDeviceCapabilities.

Done.

Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF" (#1776)

Issues.Title: [UWP] HttpClientHandler - Digest Authentication Broken on Windows 10 PC

This is specific to only the UWP HttpClientHandler. On my Windows 10 PC, the HttpClientHandler in .NET Framework 4.8 still works fine.

Like I said, this is a new issue. The System.Net.Http.HttpClientHandler on UWP definitely did support Digest up until about a week ago.

My appxbundle was built with Target version 10.0.17134, Min version 10.0.15063.

I also tested with the latest & the problem still persists; Target version 10.0.18362, Min version 10.0.18362.

WORKS

Android
iOS

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths" (#43153)

Issues.Title: Avoid duplicate Remote.Razor builds during pack
Issues.Body:
Remove `SelfContained=$(SelfContained)` from the `MSBuild` task in the `PublishBundledLanguageServer` target of `roslyn-language-server.csproj`.

When `PublishBundledLanguageServer` published `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.LanguageServer.csproj`, the `MSBuild` task forwarded `SelfContained` as a global property to transitive project references such as `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Remote.Razor.csproj`. The ARM64 `CoreComponents` VSIX reference also builds `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Remote.Razor.csproj` for the same `Configuration`, `TargetFramework`, and `RuntimeIdentifier`, without a `SelfContained` global property.

Because the global property sets differed, MSBuild created two project instances of `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Remote.Razor.csproj` that shared one intermediate output directory. In a parallel pack, both instances could compile `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Remote.Razor.dll` at the same time and fail with `CS2012`. In the default pack, removing the explicit property makes both paths use the same global properties and build a single project instance.

A focused parallel pack reproduced `CS2012` before this change. After cleaning and rebuilding the affected project, the pack succeeded and used one `win-arm64` project evaluation.

Fixes dotnet/roslyn#86467

Issues.Title: Fix file glob matching for watched files
Issues.Body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/vscode-csharp/issues/9990

`LoadedProject.Target.FilePathIsIncludedInFileGlobs` passed the full `filePath` to `matcher.Match` alongside `_projectDirectory`. On Windows, file watcher notifications from VS Code can report a lowercase drive letter while `_projectDirectory` uses an uppercase drive letter. When the drive letter casing differed, the glob matcher did not match the path. `LoadedProject` then skipped reloading the project, and the language server fell back to `FileBasedProgramsProjectSystem`.

Convert `filePath` to a project-relative path with `PathUtilities.GetRelativePath` before calling `matcher.Match`. `PathUtilities.GetRelativePath` compares path prefixes case-insensitively on Windows, so new files match the project globs regardless of drive letter casing.

Issues.Title: ProjectData: resolve shared-block framework packs per target framework
Issues.Body:
Fixes #86529

### Problem

`ProjectDataMerger` moves any list section that is identical across slices into the dimensionless shared block. Three of those sections hold *names* rather than paths, and `CacheFileReader` resolves those names against the slice's target framework:

- `[frameworkPacks]`
- `[sdkAnalyzerPacks]`
- `[sdkAnalyzerConfigPolicy]`

The shared block has no target framework, so a multi-targeted project broke in two ways:
- **Wrong reference assemblies:** every slice got the highest installed pack. With `net11.0;net8.0`, the net8.0 slice was given `ref/net11.0` reference assemblies.
- **No analysis-level config:** neither slice got its SDK `analysislevel_*_default.globalconfig`.

`ProjectDataSnapshotFactory` then merged those already-resolved results into every slice.

### Fix

The reader now hands these three sections from the shared block down to each per-TFM slice, ahead of the slice's own entries, and resolves them there. The shared slice no longer carries them, so the snapshot merge cannot reintroduce the wrong pack. The shared block's explicit references are handed down too (by file name), so they keep overriding same-named pack assemblies and analyzers exactly as before.

The change is in the reader rather than the merger, so it also corrects caches that SDKs which have already shipped write today; SDK 11.0.100 writes this shape. Stopping the merger from hoisting these sections, as #86244 does for its new pack-relative analyzer sections, would still be reasonable on top of this, but it is not needed for correctness.

### Validation

- **New tests in `CacheFileReaderTests`:**
  - shared `[frameworkPacks]` resolved per TFM (net10.0 and net8.0 pick different pack versions)
  - shared packs combined with a slice's own packs
  - shared `[sdkAnalyzerConfigPolicy]` resolved per TFM
  - an explicit reference or analyzer in the shared block still overrides the same-named pack entry in the merged snapshot. Without this, a NuGet `System.Text.Json.dll` and the pack's copy would both appear.
  - All five fail before this change and pass after. The full `Microsoft.NET.ProjectData.UnitTests` suite passes (172 tests).
- **End to end, on the `net11.0;net8.0` repro from the issue** (cache written by SDK 11.0.100, read with `ReadProjectDataSnapshotsAsync`):

  | | net8.0 `System.Runtime.dll` | net8.0 analysis-level config |
  |---|---|---|
  | before | `packs/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Ref/11.0.0/ref/net11.0/` | none |
  | after | `packs/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Ref/8.0.30/ref/net8.0/` | `analysislevel_8_default.globalconfig` |

Issues.Title: ProjectData: multi-targeted .lscache resolves shared [frameworkPacks] without a TFM, so a net8.0 slice gets net11.0 reference assemblies
Issues.Body:
### Version Used

- .NET SDK 11.0.100 (writes `version=2.2` caches)
- `Microsoft.NET.ProjectData` 5.14.0-1.26567.6 from vs-impl, and `main` at 616b2ea1b670fc279c1e6a028579c64ef94924c3

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a library that multi-targets two .NET versions and generate its cache:

   `Lib/Lib.csproj`
   ```xml
   <Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
     <PropertyGroup>
       <TargetFrameworks>net11.0;net8.0</TargetFrameworks>
     </PropertyGroup>
   </Project>
   ```

   ```sh
   dotnet build Lib -t:ProjectDataBuild -p:EnableProjectDataInProjectFolder=true
   ```

   Both TFMs need `Microsoft.NETCore.App.Ref`, so the merger hoists that section into the dimensionless shared block. The same happens to `[sdkAnalyzerConfigPolicy]`:

   ```ini
   [sourceFiles]
   Class1.cs

   [frameworkPacks]
   Microsoft.NETCore.App.Ref
   ...
   [sdkAnalyzerConfigPolicy]
   Microsoft.NET.Sdk/analyzers
   ...
   ---
   [sliceDimensions]
   TargetFramework=net11.0
   ...
   ---
   [sliceDimensions]
   TargetFramework=net8.0
   ```

2. Read the cache with the API the language server uses (`LanguageServerProjectSystem.TryLoadProjectFromCacheAsync` calls `ReadProjectDataSnapshotsAsync`):

   `read.cs`
   ```csharp
   #:package Microsoft.NET.ProjectData@5.14.0-1.26567.6
   #:property RestoreAdditionalProjectSources=https://pkgs.dev.azure.com/azure-public/vside/_packaging/vs-impl/nuget/v3/index.json
   using Microsoft.NET.ProjectData;

   string project = Path.GetFullPath(args[0]);
   var resolver = new CachePathResolver(sdkVersion: args[1]);

   // What the language server gets.
   foreach (var snapshot in await CacheFileReader.ReadProjectDataSnapshotsAsync(project, cacheInProject: true, resolver, solutionPath: null, stringPool: null, default))
   {
       var systemRuntime = snapshot.ItemsByType["MetadataReference"].Select(i => i.ItemSpec).Where(p => Path.GetFileName(p) == "System.Runtime.dll");
       Console.WriteLine($"{snapshot.Dimensions["TargetFramework"]}: {string.Join(", ", systemRuntime)}");
   }

   // The slices behind those snapshots.
   foreach (var slice in await CacheFileReader.ReadProjectCacheAsync(project, cacheInProject: true, resolver, default))
   {
       string name = slice.SliceDimensions.TryGetValue("TargetFramework", out var tfm) ? tfm : "(shared)";
       Console.WriteLine($"slice {name}: {slice.MetadataReferences.Length} metadata refs; analyzer configs: [{string.Join(", ", slice.AnalyzerConfigFiles.Select(Path.GetFileName))}]");
   }
   ```

   ```sh
   dotnet run read.cs -- Lib/Lib.csproj 11.0.100
   ```

### Expected Behavior

Each slice gets the inputs its own build passes to csc:

| TFM | `System.Runtime.dll` | SDK analysis-level config |
|---|---|---|
| net11.0 | `packs/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Ref/11.0.0/ref/net11.0/` | `analysislevel_11_default.globalconfig` |
| net8.0 | a `Microsoft.NETCore.App.Ref` 8.0.x pack, `ref/net8.0/` | `analysislevel_8_default.globalconfig` |

### Actual Behavior

```
net11.0: <dotnet>/packs/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Ref/11.0.0/ref/net11.0/System.Runtime.dll
net8.0: <dotnet>/packs/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Ref/11.0.0/ref/net11.0/System.Runtime.dll
slice (shared): 176 metadata refs; analyzer configs: []
slice net11.0: 0 metadata refs; analyzer configs: [Lib.GeneratedMSBuildEditorConfig.editorconfig]
slice net8.0: 0 metadata refs; analyzer configs: [Lib.GeneratedMSBuildEditorConfig.editorconfig]
```

- **The net8.0 project is given net11.0 reference assemblies.** A cache-loaded net8.0 project is therefore analysed against APIs that its build does not have.
- **Neither slice gets its analysis-level global config.** As a result, the SDK's default CA rule severities are missing from cache-loaded projects. This half only applies to callers that bind the resolver to an SDK; the default `new CachePathResolver()` skips `[sdkAnalyzerConfigPolicy]` entirely.

A single-target project is unaffected because it has no shared block.

### Cause

- `ProjectDataMerger.WriteMergedContent` hoists every list section that is identical across slices into the shared block ([ProjectDataMerger.cs#L258-L268](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/616b2ea1b670fc279c1e6a028579c64ef94924c3/src/ProjectData/Microsoft.NET.ProjectData.Tasks/ProjectDataMerger.cs#L258-L268)).
- Most of those sections are paths, but three are *names that are resolved against the slice's target framework*: `[frameworkPacks]`, `[sdkAnalyzerPacks]` and `[sdkAnalyzerConfigPolicy]`.
- `CacheFileReader` builds the shared block as a slice of its own. `GetTargetFramework()` returns `null` there ([CacheFileReader.cs#L964](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/616b2ea1b670fc279c1e6a028579c64ef94924c3/src/ProjectData/Microsoft.NET.ProjectData/CacheFileReader.cs#L964)), so:
  - `FindRefPackDirectory` applies no major-version filter and returns the highest installed pack.
  - `ResolveNetAnalyzersConfigFile` cannot compute a default analysis level and returns nothing.
- `ProjectDataSnapshotFactory.MergeSharedIntoSlice` then copies those already-resolved references into every TFM ([ProjectDataSnapshotFactory.cs#L75](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/616b2ea1b670fc279c1e6a028579c64ef94924c3/src/ProjectData/Microsoft.NET.ProjectData/Model/ProjectDataSnapshotFactory.cs#L75)).

#86244 hit the same problem for its new pack-relative analyzer sections ("Pack-relative analyzers must resolve with each slice's TFM, not the shared slice's absent TFM") and stops the merger hoisting them. It deliberately leaves `[frameworkPacks]` as is, so metadata references are still affected.

### Suggested fix

Have the reader hand these sections from the shared block down to each per-TFM slice and resolve them there. Fixing it in the reader also corrects caches written by SDKs that have already shipped (11.0.100 writes this shape today). Additionally, the merger could stop hoisting these sections, as #86244 does for its analyzer sections.

Issues.Title: Avoid switches over PooledArrayBuilder inline elements to work around JIT bug
Issues.Body:
Works around dotnet/roslyn#85656. The full analysis is in [this comment](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/85656#issuecomment-6969645202).

### Problem

Some .NET 10 and .NET 11 runtimes miscompile a `switch` whose value becomes a constant, for example after loop unrolling, once tiered PGO has marked one case as dominant. Every unrolled copy then jumps to the dominant case (dotnet/runtime#132370). It's fixed in 10.0.13. For .NET 11 the fix (dotnet/runtime#137375) landed after 11.0.0 shipped.

The inline-element accessors of `PooledArrayBuilder<T>` (`index switch { 0 => _element0, ... }`) are aggressively inlined, and they hit this inside `TokenizerBackedParser.Lookahead(1)`. The unrolled put-back loop reads `tokens[0]` in place of `tokens[1]`, so `ParseStatement` rewinds the source to the wrong position before handing off to the HTML parser. The HTML parser then starts `tagNameLength - 1` characters after the whitespace before the `<`. That's why the failures in the issue follow `indent < tagNameLength - 1`, and why the reported RZ1021 columns land inside tag names. It only happens in long-lived processes such as the compiler server.

### Change

- Rewrite the four switches over the inline elements as if-chains, which the JIT bug doesn't affect: `GetInlineElement`, `SetInlineElement`, `RemoveAt` and `InlineItemsToImmutableArray`. With a constant index, both forms fold to a direct field access. With a variable index, it's at most four compares instead of a jump table. I haven't benchmarked it.
- Add a comment explaining why, so nobody turns them back into switches.
- Add `PooledArrayBuilderTests.Indexer_ConstantIndexInUnrolledLoop`. It mirrors `Lookahead(1)` and runs for 1 second, which gives tiered compilation time to promote the code to Tier1 with PGO. **This test adds about 1s to the suite.**

### Why keep it after the runtime fix

- The test guards the builder that the Razor parser depends on against this kind of JIT regression. The runtime bug shipped in every .NET 10 release from preview 1 through 10.0.12, and in .NET 11 through 11.0.0, before anyone tied it to the RZ1021 reports.
- Razor also runs on runtimes that don't come bundled with the SDK, such as IDE hosts, or `Microsoft.Net.Compilers.Razor.Toolset` with an older SDK. This repo's test toolset also pins runtime 10.0.10, which is affected.

For `dotnet build`, the runtime fix is what resolves the issue. A new SDK ships with its own, fixed runtime.

### Testing

- **Runtime 11.0.0 (affected):** the new test fails 3 out of 3 runs against the old code (about 0.3s in) and passes 3 out of 3 with this change.
- **Standalone repro of the same `Lookahead(1)` + builder shape:** wrong results on 11.0.0; correct with `DOTNET_TieredPGO=0`, on runtime 10.0.15, and with if-chain accessors.
- **`Microsoft.AspNetCore.Razor.Utilities.Shared.UnitTests`:** passes on net10.0 (runtimes 10.0.15 and 11.0.0) and on net472.
- **`Microsoft.AspNetCore.Razor.Language.Legacy.UnitTests`:** passes.
- **`Microsoft.AspNetCore.Razor.Language.UnitTests`:** the same 18 failures with and without this change, caused by line endings in my local clone.
- **Not reproduced:** RZ1021 from the shipped Razor compiler in a test harness, because the inlining and unrolling profile it needs didn't line up there. The column arithmetic in the issue comment is what ties the miscompile to this code path.

Issues.Title: API proposal: SymbolDisplayPartKind.Discard
Issues.Body:
## Background and Motivation

Follow-up to https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/85256, per https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/85256#issuecomment-5736828893.

Today, C# symbol display classifies the `_` of a discard inconsistently:

- `IDiscardSymbol` (e.g. `_ = M();`, `M(out _)`, `var _`) is emitted as `SymbolDisplayPartKind.Punctuation`.
- `IParameterSymbol` with `IsDiscard == true` (e.g. `(_, _) => 1`) is emitted as `SymbolDisplayPartKind.ParameterName`, the same as a lambda parameter actually named `_` (e.g. `(_, value) => 1`).

The language spec doesn't treat `_` as punctuation. Classifying a discard parameter as `ParameterName` also drops information: the display can't tell a discard apart from a real parameter that is in scope and can be referenced. As a result, Quick Info doesn't match the editor's colors. The editor colors discards as keywords ([#28284](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/28284#issuecomment-424105872)), and Quick Info shows the same `_` in different styles depending on how it was produced.

In the PR discussion, @AlekseyTs suggested following the existing pattern where some part kinds give more specific information about an identifier (`MethodName`, `PropertyName`, etc.), and adding a dedicated kind for discards. This proposal agrees with that approach, but proposes **a single new kind, `Discard`**, instead of two (`DiscardName` and `DiscardParameterName`).

The reason for one kind is that it has come up in LDM that we might make `_` a keyword. We might make it a contextual keyword in discard positions, or we might go further and make it a full keyword everywhere, so that using it as an identifier would require escaping it as `@_`. Either way, a discard would stop being a specialized identifier. "Name" kinds split by symbol type (`DiscardName` vs. `DiscardParameterName`) would almost immediately become legacy, and we'd have two enum members describing what is really one keyword-like token. A single `Discard` kind is accurate under today's grammar, where a discard is a specialized identifier. It is also accurate under either keyword outcome, where it becomes a more specific classification of a keyword. Consumers who need to know whether a discard came from a parameter or from a discard symbol can still check `SymbolDisplayPart.Symbol`.

## Proposed API

```diff
 namespace Microsoft.CodeAnalysis
 {
     public enum SymbolDisplayPartKind
     {
         ...
         RecordClassName = 31,
         RecordStructName = 32,
+        /// <summary>A discard (e.g. "_" in <c>_ = M();</c>, <c>out _</c>, or <c>(_, _) => 1</c>).</summary>
+        Discard = 33,
     }
 }
```

Behavior changes in C# symbol display:

| Symbol | Today | Proposed |
|---|---|---|
| `IDiscardSymbol` | `Punctuation` | `Discard` |
| `IParameterSymbol` where `IsDiscard == true` | `ParameterName` | `Discard` |
| `IParameterSymbol` named `_` where `IsDiscard == false` | `ParameterName` | `ParameterName` (unchanged) |

If `_` becomes a full keyword everywhere, the last row would only apply to symbols that are declared with `@_` or that come from older language versions or from metadata. At that point, symbol display would presumably escape those names as `@_`, the same way it already escapes other identifiers that collide with keywords.

The IDE would map `SymbolDisplayPartKind.Discard` to `TextTags.Keyword`, so Quick Info and other tagged-text surfaces match editor classification. (Internal-only follow-up: `InternalSymbolDisplayPartKind`'s base and `EnumBounds.IsValid` move to `Discard`.)

## Usage Examples

```csharp
foreach (var part in symbol.ToDisplayParts())
{
    var tag = part.Kind switch
    {
        SymbolDisplayPartKind.Discard => TextTags.Keyword, // consistent with editor classification
        SymbolDisplayPartKind.ParameterName => TextTags.Parameter,
        // ...
    };
}
```

```csharp
// Distinguishing a discard from a parameter that is actually named `_`,
// without needing to inspect the symbol:
bool isDiscard = part.Kind == SymbolDisplayPartKind.Discard;
```

## Alternative Designs

1. **Two new kinds, `DiscardName` (for `IDiscardSymbol`) and `DiscardParameterName` (for discard parameters).** This fits the existing `*Name` pattern under today's grammar, where `_` is an identifier. But it has come up in LDM that we might make `_` a keyword, which would almost immediately make the "Name" framing and the split by symbol type legacy. The split also adds no information that `SymbolDisplayPart.Symbol` doesn't already provide.
2. **`SymbolDisplayPartKind.Keyword`** (the original approach in #85256). This is the simplest option, and it matches the editor, but under today's spec `_` isn't a keyword. If `_` becomes a full keyword everywhere, `Keyword` would become spec-accurate. `Discard` would still be accurate then, and it would carry more specific information, much like `AnonymousTypeIndicator` does for a keyword-like part.
3. **`SymbolDisplayPartKind.Punctuation` for all discards.** Contradicts the spec, and doesn't match the editor.
4. **`ParameterName` / `LocalName` for discards.** Follows today's grammar literally, but erases the difference between a discard and a name that is in scope. The IDE would then have to re-derive and override the compiler's classification.
5. **No change.** Keeps today's inconsistency between discard kinds and between Quick Info and the editor.

## Risks

- This changes the behavior of a public API. Consumers that switch on `SymbolDisplayPartKind` will see a new value for discards. Consumers that handle unknown kinds with a default/fallback will treat discards as plain text. Consumers that match on `Punctuation` or `ParameterName` text `_` will stop matching discards.
- Consumers that exhaustively map kinds (IDE `TextTags` mapping, documentation generators, third-party tooling) need a new case.
- If `_` later becomes a full keyword everywhere, `Discard` overlaps with `Keyword`. Consumers that already map `Discard` to `TextTags.Keyword` would be unaffected.

Issues.Title: Do not flow the Visual Studio SDK from ExternalAccess
Issues.Body:
The ExternalAccess package currently exposes the Visual Studio SDK through its LanguageServices project reference. The SDK brings in the legacy `Microsoft.VisualStudio.TaskRunnerExplorer.14.0` package, which can collide with newer Visual Studio assemblies.

Keep the SDK available when building ExternalAccess, but make it private to the package. Consumers that need SDK-provided dependencies must reference them explicitly.

A net472 consumer restored against the original package resolved both the SDK and Task Runner; neither appeared with the updated package. The consumer still compiled against LanguageServices APIs using Visual Studio interop types.

Issues.Title: Display project load diagnostics in the problems list
Issues.Body:
Currently if a project fails to load, we pop up a toast that we can't load the project. This is noisy if there's an issue that doesn't cause immediate problems (like a vulnerable NuGet package), and it also blocks other UI too. Clicking the toast still requires you to dig through the logs which is also a pain. Showing the current list of errors in the problems list is just what we should have done originally.

To ensure we always can report diagnostics, we now take an approach that if we try loading a project and get no targets back, we create an empty target without a TFM just to act as a "placeholder" to report diagnostics, since the rest of our diagnostics pipeline expects there to be a Project in the solution for diagnostics. I generally cleaned up the diagnostic handling to also put the diagnostics for a specific target into the right info object, so things are a bit clearer now, even if the resulting diff is a bit larger. As a side effect, we discovered we weren't reporting line/column numbers for MSBuild load errors, which we could have been doing this entire time but just didn't wire things up right.

Commit-at-a-time recommended.

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/vscode-csharp/issues/9965
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-dotnettools/issues/3791

Issues.Title: Use the formatting options' newline when inserting suppression pragmas
Issues.Body:
Fixes #69358

The C# suppression fixer inserted a hardcoded `CarriageReturnLineFeed` around the `#pragma warning disable/restore` directives, so the inserted lines ignored the configured `end_of_line`. Following the [direction on the issue](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/69358#issuecomment-6943379443) (the formatting options are the source of truth for line endings), this passes `SyntaxFormattingOptions.NewLine` from the pragma code actions down to the language fixers.

- **C#:** uses `EndOfLine(newLine)`. I first tried `ElasticCarriageReturnLineFeed`, as [suggested on the issue](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/69358#issuecomment-6943359972), but the elastic trivia makes the formatter reformat around the inserted directive, and 3 existing tests fail:
  - `TestFormattingDiagnosticSuppressed`: `int x = 0 ;` gets reformatted even though the fix inserts `#pragma warning disable format` around it.
  - `TestPragmaWarningDirectiveAroundTrivia1`: the comments after the directive get re-indented.
  - `TestPragmaWarningDirectiveWithDocumentationComment2`: a blank line gets removed.

  A plain end-of-line built from the options' text keeps today's behavior and drops the hardcoded CRLF.
- **VB:** already used elastic trivia. It now uses `ElasticEndOfLine(newLine)` instead of `ElasticCarriageReturnLineFeed`. A non-elastic end-of-line breaks `TestPragmaWarningDirectiveAroundTrivia6`, so VB stays elastic.

**Tests**

- Removed `Skip` from the 5 LF test cases that pointed to this issue (3 in `SuppressionTests.vb`, 2 in `SimplifyTypeNamesTests.vb`). These tests now set `FormattingOptions2.NewLine` to the line ending under test, instead of expecting the document's line endings to be kept regardless of the options.
- Turned the C# `TestInfoDiagnosticSuppressed` into an LF/CRLF theory with the same option.
- Added an optional `options` parameter to `AbstractSuppressionDiagnosticTest_NoEditor.TestAsync`. It is now `internal`, because `OptionsCollection` is internal.

Local runs on Linux (`net10.0`), compared with `main`:

| Filter | `main` | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C# Features `FullyQualifiedName~Suppression` | 291 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped | 292 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped |
| VB Features `Suppression\|SimplifyTypeNames` | 161 passed, 8 failed, 9 skipped | 171 passed, 3 failed, 4 skipped |

The 3 VB failures left (`TestSuppressionWithExistingGlobalSuppressionsDocument`, `...Document3`, `TestSuppressionWithUsingDirectiveInExistingGlobalSuppressionsDocument`) fail the same way on `main` on this machine. They are in the global-suppressions-file path, which this change does not touch.

Assisted by Claude Opus 5.5; description drafted with AI, and then reviewed and edited by the author.

Issues.Title: VB Simplifier removes a cast in an object creation argument that selects the constructor overload
Issues.Body:
**Version Used:** Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.VisualBasic.Workspaces 4.14.0

**Steps to Reproduce:**

Reduce this document (each `Return` on its own) with every node annotated with `Simplifier.Annotation` (`Simplifier.ReduceAsync(document)`), Option Strict Off:

```vb
Imports System

Public Enum Img
    None
    Info
End Enum

Public Class P
    Public V As String
    Public Sub New(i As Img)
    End Sub
    Public Sub New(s As String)
    End Sub
End Class

Public Class N
    Public V As String
    Public Sub New(i As Integer)
        V = "Integer"
    End Sub
    Public Sub New(l As Long)
        V = "Long"
    End Sub
End Class

Public Class F
    Public V As String
    Public Sub New(f As Func(Of Integer))
        V = "Integer"
    End Sub
    Public Sub New(f As Func(Of Long))
        V = "Long"
    End Sub
End Class

Public Class Test
    Public Shared Function M(o As Object, l As Long, i As Integer) As Object
        Return New P(CType(o, Img)).V
        Return New P(CType(CType(o, Img), Img)).V
        Return New N(CInt(l)).V
        Return New N(CLng(i)).V
        Return New F(Function() CInt(l)).V
    End Function
End Class
```

**Expected Behavior:** the casts are kept: each one selects the constructor.

**Actual Behavior:**

| Input | Reduced | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `New P(CType(o, Img)).V` | `New P(o).V` | BC30519 (no accessible `New` can be called without a narrowing conversion) |
| `New P(CType(CType(o, Img), Img)).V` | `New P(o).V` | BC30519; both casts are removed |
| `New N(CInt(l)).V` | `New N(l).V` | compiles, silently calls `New(Long)` |
| `New N(CLng(i)).V` | `New N(i).V` | compiles, silently calls `New(Integer)` (the removed cast is widening) |
| `New F(Function() CInt(l)).V` | `New F(Function() l).V` | compiles, silently calls `New(Func(Of Long))` (the cast picks the lambda's return type) |

The cast reducer doesn't check that the object creation still selects the same constructor without the cast. It isn't specific to narrowing conversions or Option Strict Off: the widening `CLng(i)` is removed too. Method invocations keep such casts in our tests (`P.Show(CType(o, Img))` with `Show(Img)`/`Show(String)`, `P.N(CInt(l))` with `N(Integer)`/`N(Long)`).

**Suggested fix:** for a cast in an argument of an object creation (also inside a lambda in the argument), bind the creation speculatively without the cast and keep the cast unless the same constructor is chosen without errors; check the result of removing nested casts as a whole, not each cast against the original tree.

I investigated this and wrote the report with Claude (Anthropic); I reviewed it, understand it and take responsibility for it as my own.

Issues.Title: VB Simplifier removes As clause of a local/For/For Each variable even when the name then binds to a different symbol
Issues.Body:
**Version Used:** Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.VisualBasic.Workspaces 4.14.0

**Steps to Reproduce:**

Reduce this document with every node annotated with `Simplifier.Annotation` (`Simplifier.ReduceAsync(document)`), Option Strict Off, Option Infer On, reference to Microsoft.VisualBasic:

```vb
Imports Microsoft.VisualBasic

Public Class Icon
    Public Shared Function FromHandle(h As Integer) As Icon
        Return Nothing
    End Function
    Public Shared Function All() As Icon()
        Return {}
    End Function
End Class

Public Class C
    Private i As Integer
    Public Property Company As String
    Public Shared Companies As String() = {}

    Public Sub Test()
        For month As Integer = 1 To 12 : Next
        For i As Integer = 0 To 2 : Next
        Dim icon As Icon = Icon.FromHandle(1)
        For Each company As String In Companies : Next
    End Sub

    Public Sub Test2()
        For Each icon As Icon In Icon.All() : Next
    End Sub
End Class
```

**Expected Behavior:** the document compiles and means the same after reduction; the `As` clauses are kept where removing them would change binding.

**Actual Behavior:** the input has no errors; after reduction (whole document, or each statement on its own) each row fails as shown:

| Input | Reduced | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `For month As Integer = 1 To 12` | `For month = 1 To 12` | BC30455 (`month` binds to `DateAndTime.Month`) |
| `For i As Integer = 0 To 2` | `For i = 0 To 2` | compiles, but the loop now uses the field `i` |
| `Dim icon As Icon = Icon.FromHandle(1)` | `Dim icon = Icon.FromHandle(1)` | BC30980 (type of `icon` can't be inferred from an expression containing `icon`) |
| `For Each company As String In Companies` | `For Each company In Companies` | BC30039 (`company` binds to the `Company` property, which can't be a loop control variable) |
| `For Each icon As Icon In Icon.All()` | `For Each icon In Icon.All` | BC30980 |

`VisualBasicVariableDeclaratorReducer.TryReduceVariableDeclaratorWithoutType` compares the declared type with the initializer's type (locals/`Using`), with the `To` type (`For`), or checks an identity conversion (`For Each`), but never checks what the name binds to once `As` is gone:
- a `For`/`For Each` control variable without `As` reuses a symbol of that name in scope (anything but a type or type parameter, see `ForOrForEachBlockBinder.BuildLocals`) instead of declaring a new local;
- an inferred local is in scope in its own initializer (and a `For Each` variable in its collection), so a member access on a type of the same name (allowed with `As T` by the "Color Color" rule) now binds to the local.

`SimplificationOptions.PreferImplicitTypeInLocalDeclaration` used to make the reducer keep `As` clauses. It has been obsolete and unused since #40544 (merged 2020-01-04, Roslyn 3.5), and there is no replacement.

**Suggested fix:** in the reducer, speculatively bind the declaration without `As` (or look up the name outside the declaring block for `For`/`For Each`) and keep the clause when the name would refer to an existing symbol, or when the initializer refers to a type or namespace of the same name.

Issues.Title: Add discovery-before-generation and AI-enablement gap guidance for agents
Issues.Body:
🤖Copilot🤖
Part of the AI Engineering Checklist epic #55185 (not closing it). This PR covers two checklist items:

- **Tier 3, P0:** "Add an explicit discovery-before-generation step to agent instructions/skills (read nearby code + conventions before writing), distinct from Tier 1 documentation."
- **Tier 2, P1:** "Treat missing test hooks, opaque runtime state, and unstructured signals as AI-enablement gaps in the backlog."

## Changes

- **Root `AGENTS.md`, new "Before writing code" section.** Before generating code, agents do the following:
  - Read the nearest area `AGENTS.md` and the skill that owns the task.
  - Find the closest sibling implementation and its tests, and follow that pattern. If they deliberately diverge, they state why.
  - Check whether the same change also belongs in sibling implementations, parallel templates, or shared test assets.
  - Check recent `git log` history for reverted approaches and in-flight migrations.

  Today these checks exist only in fragments: `code-review`, `analyze-sdk-issue`, and `add-cli-command`. This section makes them a repo-wide step and keeps it separate from the memory/orientation guidance.
- **Root `AGENTS.md`, new "Reporting AI-enablement gaps" section.** When an agent hits a missing test hook, opaque runtime state, or an unstructured signal, it does not silently work around it and does not grow the change to build the missing infrastructure. Instead, its final handoff includes a ready-to-file issue title and body for an `Area-AIEngineering` issue, with the evidence.
- **`run-tests` skill.** After the diagnostics guidance, one paragraph links to the gap section for cases where the TRX, binlogs, and output still don't explain a failure.

## Open for reviewer input: filing policy

The current text uses **option A**: the agent reports the gap with a ready-to-file title and body, searches for an existing issue first, and files only when the user asks. The alternatives are:

- **B:** the agent searches for an existing issue, then files directly.
- **C (hybrid):** interactive sessions recommend filing, and unattended/CI agents that are already allowed to create issues (gh-aw safe-outputs) file directly.

Option A was picked as the conservative default. It matches the existing norm that agents don't open PRs unless asked, it avoids duplicate issues from parallel sessions, and it doesn't assume agents have label permissions. Feedback on A vs. B/C is welcome.

## Validation

- All 25 local Markdown links and anchors in the changed files resolve, which is what `check-markdown-links` checks.
- I went through the `update-docs` checklist. No memory, index, or convention-owner updates are needed, and the existing anchors into `AGENTS.md` are unchanged.

This is a docs/agent-guidance change only, with no product or user-visible behavior change.

Issues.Title: Adopt a correct-once principle for recurring agent failures
Issues.Body:
🤖Copilot🤖
Part of epic #55185, for the item **"(P1) Adopt a correct-once principle: recurring agent failures are fixed in the harness (instructions/skills/tests/analyzers), not only in the current PR."**

## Changes

- **Root `AGENTS.md`** ("Keeping AI context and docs in sync"): adds a short correct-once statement. When a task fixes a recurring agent failure, also fix the cause in the harness (the owning `AGENTS.md`, skill, memory file, test, or analyzer). The statement defers to `update-docs` for where each kind of fix belongs.
- **`update-docs` skill**: adds a checklist item, *"Corrected a recurring agent failure?"* It prefers an enforceable test or analyzer and falls back to the nearest `AGENTS.md`, the owning skill, or the matching memory file. It excludes one-off mistakes.

## Scope and relationship to the review-comment loop

This change only states the principle and says where fixes belong. It does not cover how recurring failures are detected or collected.

Epic #55185 also has a separate, in-progress item: **"(P1) Add a review-comment-to-harness loop: recurring comments become instructions, tests, analyzer rules, or skills."** This PR leaves detection and intake to that work, which can later add review comments as one source of recurring failures without rewriting this text. If you own the review-comment loop, please fold this into your change or adjust the wording to fit your design. I'm happy to close this PR in favor of yours.

Issues.Title: Validate agent skills in CI
Issues.Body:
🤖Copilot🤖
Part of #55185 (partial): advances the P1 item **"Give AI artifacts owners and review expectations like source code; add a DRY/stale-artifact audit cadence and a retirement path"** by enforcing skill validation in CI. The audit cadence and retirement-path documentation are out of scope and are handled separately.

## Changes

- **New workflow** [`.github/workflows/validate-skills.yml`](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/miyanni-validate-skills-in-ci/.github/workflows/validate-skills.yml): runs on pull requests that touch `.github/skills/**` (including `ValidateSkill.cs`), `.claude/skills/**`, or the workflow itself. It also supports manual dispatch. It installs the repo-pinned SDK via `eng/common/dotnet.sh`, runs `ValidateSkill.cs` on every skill directory in **both** `.github/skills` and `.claude/skills`, emits a `::error file=…/SKILL.md::` annotation for each failure, and fails if any skill fails. `DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_SESSIONID` is set at workflow scope, as required by root `AGENTS.md`.
- **`ValidateSkill.cs`**: adds `#:property RollForward=LatestMajor`. The pinned SDK (12.0 alpha) builds file-based apps for `net11.0`, but it only includes the 12.0 runtime. Without a full restore, the validator could not launch from the repo root.
- **`migrate-xunit-to-mstest`**: was 551 lines and exceeded the spec's 500-line limit. Step 11's detailed parallelization tables, alternative models, opt-out translation, diagnosis, and `xunit.runner.json` migration moved to `references/parallelization.md`. The recommended Choice A attribute and its REQUIRED user-facing explanation stay in `SKILL.md` (now 472 lines).
- **`.github/skills/AGENTS.md`**: documents CI enforcement and how to reproduce locally with `./.dotnet/dotnet`.

## Validation

- All 15 skills (9 in `.github/skills`, 6 in `.claude/skills`) pass locally with the pinned SDK. Before this change, only `migrate-xunit-to-mstest` failed.
- I ran the workflow's PowerShell loop locally. It exits 0 when all skills are valid. When I renamed a skill's `name` in a test, it exits 1 with the expected error annotation.

Ownership is already covered by `CODEOWNERS` (`.github/`, `.claude/` → @mthalman, @lbussell).
