Issues.Title: Document AI artifact ownership, change intake, review, and retirement
Issues.Body:
🤖Copilot🤖
Part of the AI-readiness epic https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/55185 (Tier 5). This PR addresses:

- **(P1) Create a lightweight intake for AI artifact updates (who updates instructions/skills, and how).**
- **(P1) Give AI artifacts owners and review expectations like source code; add a DRY/stale-artifact audit cadence and a retirement path.** This PR covers ownership, review expectations, the retirement path, and a **proposed** audit cadence that still needs owner agreement (see below).

## Changes

- New [`documentation/project-docs/ai-artifacts.md`](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/miyanni-ai-artifact-intake-ownership-doc/documentation/project-docs/ai-artifacts.md):
  - **Artifact types:** root and area `AGENTS.md`, `.github/memory`, `.github/skills` and `.claude/skills`, `.github/agents`, agentic workflow sources, and `.github/copilot/settings.json`.
  - **Ownership:** `CODEOWNERS` is the source of truth. Its unanchored `AGENTS.md` and `SKILL.md` patterns come after the area entries, so they also take precedence for area instruction files. Changes to area-specific guidance also need a review from that area's owners.
  - **Intake:** anyone can propose a change. Open a PR directly for a known fix, open an `Area-AIEngineering` issue for a problem without a fix or for a new skill, agent, or workflow, or fix the artifact in the same PR when a code change makes it stale.
  - **Review and validation expectations:** grounded claims, a single source of truth, link checks, `ValidateSkill.cs`, memory `INDEX.md` sync, `gh aw compile` lock regeneration, and a behavior trial for skills, agents, and workflows.
  - **Retirement path:** triggers, a delete-don't-deprecate policy, reference cleanup in the same PR, and an issue when retirement is uncertain.
- One-line links from root `AGENTS.md` and `.github/skills/AGENTS.md`, plus entries in `documentation/README.md` and the `CONVENTIONS.md` canonical-owner table.

The review-comment-to-harness loop is a separate epic item. This doc only points to the epic for it.

## Audit cadence (proposed; needs owner agreement)

The doc adds a **proposed** quarterly review of all AI artifacts by the `CODEOWNERS` AI owners. It checks for stale claims, duplicated content, retirement candidates, and memory `INDEX.md` drift. The doc marks this cadence as proposed and not yet committed.

- **@mthalman and @lbussell: please confirm whether you agree to own this cadence**, or suggest a different interval or owner. The project coordinator chose this option while the requester was unavailable.
- **Possible follow-up:** a scheduled agentic audit workflow, modeled on `stale-reference-check`, that files bounded issues for stale or duplicated AI artifacts. It would need a new workflow, PAT-pool usage, and an owner, so it is not part of this PR.

## Validation

All local Markdown links and heading anchors in the changed files, and in all `.github/memory/*.md` files, resolve.

Issues.Title: Unblock SDK testing on Azure Linux 4 Helix VMs
Issues.Body:
We want to move SDK Linux tests to Azure Linux 4 Helix VMs, but the initial run of #57197 failed because the test process could not find git.

## Validated failure

Build 1687979 ran the Linux test job on azurelinux.4.amd64.open with no container. The Microsoft.NET.Infrastructure.Tests.dll.1 work item failed: 20 EvaluateConditionalTestScopesTests could not initialize their temporary Git repositories. The exception was:

```text
System.ComponentModel.Win32Exception: An error occurred trying to start process 'git' [...] No such file or directory
```

This concerns the **Azure Linux 4 Helix VM images**, not the Azure Linux build-agent images or NativeAOT cross-build containers.

- Build: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/cbb18261-c48f-4abb-8651-8cdcb5474649/_build/results?buildId=1687979
- Helix job metadata (queue and empty DockerTag): https://helix.dot.net/api/2019-06-17/jobs/30dd8c4f-4570-43bb-93b2-1360687e90fd/details
- Failing test log: https://helix.dot.net/api/jobs/30dd8c4f-4570-43bb-93b2-1360687e90fd/workitems/Microsoft.NET.Infrastructure.Tests.dll.1/files/console.8742732d.log?api-version=2019-06-17
- Test fixture invoking Git: https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/36379d5f0c29296da08c334b805953d455eb79fe/test/Microsoft.NET.Infrastructure.Tests/EvaluateConditionalTestScopesTests.cs#L642

## Options

We need to do one of the following:

1. **Add git to the Azure Linux 4 Helix VM images**, making it available on PATH for SDK tests.
2. **Switch back to container testing** on the Azure Linux 4 Helix VMs, using a test container that includes git and the other SDK test prerequisites. This requires re-enabling and validating the currently disabled container-based SDK test path. The SDK pipeline comment links the disabled path to this closed issue: https://github.com/dotnet/dnceng/issues/6000

#57197 currently uses Ubuntu 24.04 Helix queues instead. Its later Ubuntu test failures are separate from the missing-git failure documented here.

Issues.Title: CA1822 flags ASP.NET Core controller actions in projects that do not use Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web
Issues.Body:
## Describe the bug

CA1822 (Mark members as static) only skips externally visible members when the project is a web project, which `CompilationExtensions.IsWebProject` decides from the MSBuild property `UsingMicrosoftNETSdkWeb` (or legacy web
`ProjectTypeGuids`). It never checks whether a member is an ASP.NET Core controller action.

I have controllers are declared in a class library (`Microsoft.NET.Sdk`) that references a project that uses `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web` 
so `ASP.NET Core` is available but not specified in this project. Hence, every public action that doesn't touch instance state is reported, and applying the code fix makes the action `static`, which MVC ignores.

| Project | SDK | `UsingMicrosoftNETSdkWeb` | CA1822 on a stateless public action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Web host | `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web` | `true` | Not reported |
| Class library with the same controller | `Microsoft.NET.Sdk` | not set | **Reported** |

## Steps to reproduce

`.editorconfig` raises the rule to a warning:

```ini
[*.cs]
dotnet_diagnostic.CA1822.severity = warning
```

`ControllerLibrary/ControllerLibrary.csproj`:

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <FrameworkReference Include="Microsoft.AspNetCore.App" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

`ControllerLibrary/ClockController.cs`:

```csharp
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

[ApiController]
[Route("api/clock")]
public class ClockController : ControllerBase
{
    [HttpGet]
    public string Get([FromServices] TimeProvider time) => time.GetUtcNow().ToString("O");
}
```

Run `dotnet build`.

## Expected behavior

No CA1822 for `ClockController.Get`: ASP.NET Core requires actions to be instance methods.

## Actual behavior

```
ControllerLibrary\ClockController.cs(8,19): warning CA1822: Member 'Get' does not access instance data and can be marked as static
```

## Are there any workarounds?

| Workaround | Drawback |
|---|---|
| Set `<UsingMicrosoftNETSdkWeb>true</UsingMicrosoftNETSdkWeb>` in the library | Misrepresents the project; skips *all* public members, not only actions. |
| `dotnet_diagnostic.CA1822.severity = none` for controller folders, or `dotnet_code_quality.CA1822.api_surface = private, internal` | Loses the rule for real candidates. |
| `[SuppressMessage]` / `#pragma` per action | Noise on every stateless action; easy to forget, and the fix is offered in the IDE. |

## Proposal

CA1822 should skip members that ASP.NET Core would treat as controller actions, independent of the project SDK, by applying ASP.NET Core's own rules through `WellKnownTypeProvider`. The rule only applies when `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.ControllerAttribute` resolves in the compilation, so projects without ASP.NET Core MVC are unaffected. `WellKnownTypeNames` already defines `MicrosoftAspNetCoreMvcControllerAttribute`, `MicrosoftAspNetCoreMvcNonControllerAttribute` and `MicrosoftAspNetCoreMvcNonActionAttribute`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "CA1822 flags ASP.NET Core controller actions in projects that do not use Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web" (#57207)

Issues.Title: Reuse verified deterministic application layers when publishing containers
Issues.Body: Publishing an unchanged application currently compresses its application layer again on every container publish. Reuse deterministic layers when `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` is set, validating the canonical source tar fingerprint and both compressed and uncompressed cached-blob digests before a hit. Changed inputs invalidate reuse; layer writes and metadata replacement remain atomic and cancellable. `ContainerLayerNoIncremental=true` disables this reuse when an image is built. The independent whole-archive cache retains its separate `ContainerArchiveNoIncremental` opt-out. In local Linux x64 full-publish measurements, unchanged 200 MiB applications took 68–77% less time with layer reuse: The 4 MiB warm controls took 4.5–9.8% less time. Fresh-cache and same-length changed-content miss medians ranged from 2.4% longer to 4.1% shorter. [Controls chart](https://github.com/jetersen/dotnet-sdk/releases/download/container-application-layer-cache-evidence-ffce076d03/application-layer-controls-3068def37f.png). Seven alternating pairs per warm case and five per miss cover single/multi architecture and both MSBuild MT settings. The same complete SDK 12 ReadyToRun layout publishes a net11 app with caching toggled, a fixed epoch, and a warm loopback registry/base store. Restore, setup and verification are excluded. These are local results, not production CI gains; SDK 11 task hosting and NativeAOT applicability remain unvalidated. Task execution mode is unchanged. [Raw timings, reproduction scripts, source patch and toolchain](https://github.com/jetersen/dotnet-sdk/releases/download/container-application-layer-cache-evidence-ffce076d03/application-layer-cache-3068def37f-evidence.zip). Every publish verifies raw OCI blob hashes, original descriptor sizes/reference closure, gzip integrity and complete diff-IDs, with exact image graph equality between cache settings. Timings are pinned to `3068def37f`. The reviewed head `ffce076d03` adds optional metadata I/O/cleanup hardening and regression/test-isolation fixes, supplied as a [separate patch](https://github.com/jetersen/dotnet-sdk/releases/download/container-application-layer-cache-evidence-ffce076d03/application-layer-review-fixes-3068-to-ffce.patch) with [provenance and later native validation](https://github.com/jetersen/dotnet-sdk/releases/download/container-application-layer-cache-evidence-ffce076d03/application-layer-reviewed-head-provenance.json); no current-head timing claim. Reviewed in three sol-loop rounds with gpt-6.2-sol, xhigh; final verdict approved. Created with gpt-6.1-sol in T3 Code.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Reuse verified deterministic application layers when publishing containers" (#57206)

Issues.Title: CA2026 autofix generating non-compiling code
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

[CA2026](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/fundamentals/code-analysis/quality-rules/ca2026) raises a warning when using JsonDocument.Parse(...).RootElement and suggests using JsonElement.Parse(...) instead.  The autofix for this generates non-compiling code.  

### Steps to reproduce

Write code that uses the incorrect pattern.

```lang=C#
var root = JsonDocument.Parse(response).RootElement;
```

Run the auto-fix.  The below is the result, which does not compile:

```lang=C#
var root = JsonElement.Parse(response, JsonDocument.Parse(response));
```

### Expected behavior

The autofix should not place in an invented value for the JsonDocumentOptions optional value.  It should leave that blank, or conceivably include an options value if one is already present in the file.

Below is what I would expect to see from the autofix.

```lang=C#
var root = JsonElement.Parse(response);
```

### Actual behavior

The below is the result, which does not compile:

```lang=C#
var root = JsonElement.Parse(response, JsonDocument.Parse(response));
```

_No response_

Issues.Title: Add Local static web asset mode for server browser tools
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Introduce `AssetMode=Local`: assets remain available to their own project but are never exported through project references, regardless of `StaticWebAssetProjectMode`. Preserve existing `All`, `CurrentProject`, and `Reference` behavior.

Use `Local` for server Web SDK Hot Reload browser-tools assets to fix #56656. Keep WebAssembly browser-tools assets propagating to their hosting server. Reuse the shared reference-export predicate and existing endpoint projection rather than adding browser-tools-specific filtering or target hooks.

Add focused lifecycle and integration coverage for validation, serialization, compression, local build/publish availability, reference exclusion, ordinary initializer propagation, and hosted WebAssembly. Update related documentation and manifest baselines.

## Validation

- Full isolated Debug redist SDK build succeeded with zero warnings or errors.
- 132 focused tests passed, followed by 5 strengthened assertion reruns.
- 35 affected baseline checks passed after regeneration and rebuilding embedded resources.
- Plain API-to-API Debug build and publish succeeded with `ReferenceOutputAssembly=true` and `false`; each project retained its own three browser-tools primaries, gzip alternatives, and serving endpoints, with no browser tools in publish output.
- All three browser-tools modules returned HTTP 200 from the running application.
- Restoring `All` mode reproduced the original missing-initializer-endpoints failure.

The 37 regenerated manifest snapshots contain only 222 `All`-to-`Local` metadata changes; unrelated ordering churn was removed.

Issues.Title: Clarify dotnetup PATH configuration reporting
Issues.Body:
`dotnetup env show` and `env set` presented the saved `dotnetupOnPath` setting as the current state of `PATH`. This was misleading when the configured and observed environments differed.

- **Clarify configuration intent**
  - Rename the `env show` field from `dotnetup on PATH` to `add dotnetup to PATH`.
  - Phrase `env set` outcomes as configured behavior rather than observed state.
  - Explicitly report when dotnet access is enabled while dotnetup remains configured not to be added.

  ```text
  add dotnetup to PATH  false
  Configured to add dotnet to PATH. dotnetup is configured not to be added.
  ```

- **Keep drift reporting authoritative**
  - Preserve the separate environment inspection that reports differences between saved configuration and the persisted environment.

- **Update supporting content**
  - Add focused coverage for configuration-oriented output.
  - Update design examples and generated localization resources.

Issues.Title: extend CA2259 to attributes with no effect
Issues.Body:
fixes dotnet/runtime#131094

as approved in API review, CA2259 now reports attributes that have no effect, and says why:
- [ThreadStatic], [ContextStatic] and [FixedAddressValueType] on an instance field
- [FixedAddressValueType] on a static field of a reference type
- [SuppressGCTransition] on a method that is not a P/Invoke

`[LibraryImport]` methods and `[GeneratedComInterface]` interface methods are skipped, since the interop source generators forward `[SuppressGCTransition]` from them ([ComInterfaceGenerator.cs](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/7066044546b54c4a84bd88a84d52bab5f09e603a/src/libraries/System.Runtime.InteropServices/gen/ComInterfaceGenerator/ComInterfaceGenerator.cs#L186)). category and level are unchanged.

tested: C# and VB tests, and a build of runtime's CoreLib and libraries with the rule on: no hits.

Issues.Title: `dotnetup` env show and `env set` unclearly report a saved setting rather than the reality of `PATH`
Issues.Body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I have read the [dotnetup documentation](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/tree/release/dnup/documentation/general/dotnetup).
- [x] I have searched for [existing dotnetup issues](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aopen%20label%3AArea-dotnetup).
- [x] I have searched for [existing dotnetup discussions](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/discussions/categories/dotnetup).

### Issue type

Bug report

### Description

These strings come from the saved dotnetup-on-PATH setting, not from checking the real PATH:

`dotnetup on PATH false` / `dotnet is on your PATH. dotnetup is not.`

They seem to cause confusion that this represents whether dotneutp is on the path. We cant actually accurately detect that. We should instead make the messaging more clear that this is about whether dotnetup has a configuration setting, set to try to set itself onto the path, rather than making it affirm that it is or isn't on the path. 

 When env set turns on dotnet access without the flag, also turn dotnetup-on-PATH back on, or at least say it's being left off.

Issues.Title: `dotnetup` should not rely on `$SHELL` for the default shell
Issues.Body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I have read the [dotnetup documentation](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/tree/release/dnup/documentation/general/dotnetup).
- [x] I have searched for [existing dotnetup issues](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aopen%20label%3AArea-dotnetup).
- [x] I have searched for [existing dotnetup discussions](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/discussions/categories/dotnetup).

### Issue type

Bug report

### Description

The launch shell is often `zsh` on mac even if the user actually uses `pwsh`. If `dotnetup` was launched from a shell, we can make some assumptions that are _more_ correct than $SHELL:


Step 1: 
- Walk up the parent processes and stop at the first supported shell (bash, zsh, fish, pwsh). Walking past the immediate parent handles cases like sudo, env, make, script or a wrapper script.

Suggestion: (Needs further investigation)
      • Linux: read the parent ID from /proc/<pid>/stat and the program from /proc/<pid>/exe or comm.
      • macOS: there's no /proc, so use the native sysctl/proc_pidpath APIs.

Step 2:
-  Shell-specific environment variables (weak). ZSH_VERSION, BASH_VERSION and FISH_VERSION aren't exported, so a child process can't see them. pwsh sets PSModulePath, but child processes inherit it, so bash started from pwsh would look like pwsh. Use this only as a tiebreaker.

Step 3:
-  $SHELL as the final fallback

This still wont work when dotnetup runs from an IDE task, cron, ssh host dotnetup or a nested shell.

This only should happen in init / env set, and not in `env script` which runs all of the time. If we support writing to multiple shells as suggested that also defers the demand for this fix: https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/53963

### dotnetup version

_No response_

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-118740 - Aspire Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Aspire. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Aspire Dashboard's unauthenticated NotFound route can permit telemetry deletion in both standalone and AppHost-hosted deployments. In standalone deployments using browser-token authentication, it can also expose the browser token. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22148 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Critical - **Score:** 9.1 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N` - **Weakness:** CWE-862 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire Dashboard Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- Aspire Dashboard | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 Both 13.6.3 and 13.6.4 contain the unauthenticated NotFound route. ### Aspire Dashboard SDK packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-musl-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-musl-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Aspire Dashboard releases through 13.6.4 are affected, whether deployed independently or launched by an Aspire AppHost. For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, check the resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk package versions against the affected ranges above. If the AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, check the version of that Dashboard instead. Aspire ships independently of .NET; installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not replace the Dashboard. ### How do I fix the issue? Update Aspire Dashboard to version 13.6.5 or later. Neither 13.6.3 nor 13.6.4 is a fixed upgrade target. For container deployments, explicitly set the Dashboard image to `mcr.microsoft.com/aspire/dashboard:13.6.5` and recreate or redeploy the container. Replace older version tags and nightly image references, including those in generated Docker Compose or Kubernetes manifests, with this fixed stable image. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace an image reference in an existing deployment manifest. For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, update any explicit Aspire.Hosting.AppHost version, including a central package version, to 13.6.5 or later. If that reference is supplied implicitly by Aspire.AppHost.Sdk, update the SDK reference to 13.6.5 or later instead. Restore and rebuild the AppHost, verify that its resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk packages are 13.6.5 or later, and restart the AppHost to run the updated Dashboard. If your AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, update the Dashboard in that selected bundle or location to 13.6.5 or later and restart the AppHost. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace that Dashboard. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. ASP.NET Core Identity scaffolding templates use the request-supplied email instead of the account's stored email for password-reset and confirmation messages. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/Scaffolding/issues/3959 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.1 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-640 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages Updating scaffolding packages/tools does not repair previously generated application code. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc contains the affected templates. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design is a parent package that brings in the MVC generator through a minimum-version dependency. For Design, applicability depends on the resolved MVC generator: a project that independently resolves a fixed MVC version does not become vulnerable merely because it retains an older Design reference. ### 8.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.23 | 8.0.24 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.23 | 8.0.24 ### 9.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.12 | 9.0.13 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.12 | 9.0.13 ### 10.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.2 | 10.0.3 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.2 | 10.0.3 ### Additional known affected scaffolding prereleases These are exact known affected versions, not continuous prerelease intervals. Version 20.3.0 supports .NET 8, 9, 10 and 11. Install it as a .NET tool, not as a project package reference. The MVC and Design project packages use the separate fixed versions listed above; 20.3.0 is not a version of those packages. ### Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.x Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold) | >= 20.0.0-preview.1.26156.3, <= 20.1.0 | 20.3.0 The 20.x tool contains the vulnerable Identity and Blazor templates for .NET 8.0 through 11.0. ### Affected legacy prereleases The following exact versions also contain affected templates: - [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) and [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design): `11.0.0-preview.1.26156.3` and `11.0.0-preview.1.26230.3`. - [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet): `10.0.0-rc.1.25458.5` and `10.0.0-rc.1.25468.1`. Apply the generated-code repair below to applications created with these versions. For new scaffolding, use the Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.3.0 tool, which supports .NET 8 through 11. Migrating to that tool is not an update to an MVC or Design project package reference and does not repair previously generated code. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Check both the installed scaffolding package/tool version and the code it generated. Applications generated with an affected template remain affected after the tool is updated unless their handlers are corrected. The `dotnet-aspnet-codegenerator` command loads generators from the application's dependencies. Check the project's Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design and Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc references against the versions above; updating only the command-line tool does not replace those project dependencies. For applications created with `dotnet new`, check the selected SDK with `dotnet --version` in the working directory. Use `dotnet new list` to identify available templates and `dotnet new uninstall` without arguments to list separately installed template packages. Web ProjectTemplates can be bundled with an SDK or installed separately; a project package reference alone does not identify which template generated the application. ### How do I fix the issue? Update affected scaffolding packages/tools and project dependencies to the patched versions above before generating additional code. Updating scaffolding packages/tools does not repair previously generated applications. Change generated ForgotPassword and ResendEmailConfirmation handlers, including Blazor equivalents, to send only to the stored email returned for the located user; reject missing stored addresses, rebuild and redeploy affected apps. For an existing global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold installation, update the tool: ```shell dotnet tool update --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold --version 20.3.0 ``` For Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet installations, uninstall the old tool and install its replacement: ```shell dotnet tool uninstall --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet dotnet tool install --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold --version 20.3.0 ``` For a new installation, use the install command alone. For local tools, use `--local` instead of `--global` and run the commands from the directory containing the tool manifest. Visual Studio installs and uses the updated scaffolding tool automatically; command-line installations must be updated separately. Visual Studio 17.14 uses the legacy CodeGeneration packages listed above; keep Visual Studio updated and check independently maintained project dependencies. For SDK-bundled templates, install and select an updated SDK that includes the corrected ProjectTemplates version; check `global.json` if an older SDK remains selected. Update separately installed template packs independently. Updating the SDK does not necessarily replace a separately installed template pack. For the affected legacy prereleases, correct the generated handlers before using or deploying the generated application. #### Manual repair for generated Identity handlers This repair also applies to applications generated with the affected 11.0 scaffolding packages and Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet 10.0 RC versions above; it does not require migrating to a different scaffolding tool. In the generated `ForgotPassword` and `ResendEmailConfirmation` handlers, retain the existing user lookup, missing-user responses, password-reset confirmation checks, token generation and callback-URL encoding. After those user checks, retrieve the email from the located account before sending: ```csharp var storedEmail = await UserManager.GetEmailAsync(user); if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(storedEmail)) { throw new InvalidOperationException("Users must have an email."); } ``` In Razor Pages handlers, use `_userManager` instead of `UserManager`. Replace only the recipient argument `Input.Email` with `storedEmail` in `_emailSender.SendEmailAsync`, `EmailSender.SendPasswordResetLinkAsync` and `EmailSender.SendConfirmationLinkAsync`, as applicable. Keep `Input.Email` for the account lookup; do not use it as the message recipient. Apply the change to both handlers, including their Blazor equivalents, then rebuild and redeploy. Reapply the repair if affected templates generate the handlers again. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. Issues.Body: > **Announcement consolidated:** See the [November 2026 .NET Runtime security announcement](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/498) and [shared feedback thread](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/137280). This original CVE post is retained for existing links. Closing it does not withdraw the advisory or its remediation guidance. ## Executive Summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Crafted PDB line metadata can exceed the caller-provided buffer and cause a heap out-of-bounds write. ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.8 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-122 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows - **Architectures:** x86, x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages On Windows x86, x64, and Arm64, Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native versions earlier than 18.9.1-beta1.26515.1 are affected when reading crafted native PDBs. ### .NET on Windows Product | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- .NET 8.0 installed on Windows | >= 8.0.0, < 8.0.34 | 8.0.34 .NET 9.0 installed on Windows | >= 9.0.0, < 9.0.23 | 9.0.23 .NET 10.0 installed on Windows | >= 10.0.0, < 10.0.15 | 10.0.15 .NET 11.0 installed on Windows | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0 | 11.0.0 ### Windows self-contained runtime packs These runtime packs deliver the .NET runtime for Windows self-contained applications. Applications using Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native versions earlier than 18.9.1-beta1.26515.1 on Windows x86, x64, and Arm64 to read crafted native PDBs are exposed. See [affected packages](#affected-packages) for the affected .NET products on Windows. ### How do I fix the issue? Update affected .NET installations and each installed SDK feature band to the versions listed above or later. If an SDK was installed through Visual Studio, update Visual Studio as well. For applications that deploy their own affected .NET runtime, including self-contained applications, update the runtime used to build the application, rebuild, and redeploy. Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in the Aspire CLI. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. An insecure temporary directory used by Aspire CLI-generated builds can allow a local attacker to influence MSBuild response-file discovery and execute code with the privileges of the developer running the CLI. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22101 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.3 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-379 (Creation of Temporary File in Directory with Insecure Permissions) - **MSRC severity:** Important ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire CLI Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Aspire.Cli](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli) | >= 13.2.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-arm64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-musl-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-musl-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.osx-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.osx-arm64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 ### Aspire CLI npm packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [@microsoft/aspire-cli](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-arm64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-arm64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-musl-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-musl-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-arm64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-arm64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 The affected scenario concerns CLI-generated server and integration builds on non-Windows systems when a local attacker can influence automatic MSBuild response-file discovery through an attacker-writable directory. This includes builds started by `aspire sdk generate`, `aspire sdk dump`, and `aspire sdk export`. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? The reported scenario involves a local attacker influencing a generated build through a shared temporary-directory ancestor while another user invokes the Aspire CLI. Versions 13.2.0 through 13.6.4 are affected. Aspire ships independently of .NET. Installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not establish that the affected Aspire CLI has been updated. ### How do I fix the issue? Update the Aspire CLI to version 13.6.5 or later. If installed as a .NET tool, update the Aspire.Cli package. If installed using npm, update @microsoft/aspire-cli to version 13.6.5 or later; its platform-specific dependency must also resolve to version 13.6.5 or later. Otherwise update the CLI through its installation method. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue in the [Aspire repository](https://github.com/microsoft/aspire). ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-120006 - Aspire Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Aspire. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Disclosure of an Aspire Dashboard authentication cookie to a linked service can allow an attacker-controlled container to replay the authenticated session and execute code as the host developer. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22092 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-201 (Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** macOS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Aspire.Hosting.AppHost](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Hosting.AppHost) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Hosting](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Hosting) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 The affected scenario involves a Dashboard-authenticated AppHost workflow with an attacker-controlled container and a linked HTTPS YARP gateway. The affected hosting code is in `Aspire.Hosting`, a dependency of `Aspire.Hosting.AppHost`. `Aspire.AppHost.Sdk` supplies the AppHost package implicitly unless the project overrides the default references. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? The reported scenario involves a developer starting an Aspire AppHost, authenticating to its Dashboard, and following a resource link that routes to an attacker-controlled container. All released versions through 13.6.4 are affected. Aspire ships independently of .NET. Installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not establish that the affected Aspire components have been updated. ### How do I fix the issue? Update the AppHost project's `Aspire.Hosting.AppHost` package reference to version 13.6.5 or later. If the project obtains this package implicitly through `Aspire.AppHost.Sdk`, update that SDK reference to version 13.6.5 or later. Explicit package references or central version pins must also resolve `Aspire.Hosting` to version 13.6.5 or later. Restore dependencies, rebuild, and restart the AppHost after updating. Updating only the .NET runtime, .NET SDK, Aspire CLI, or standalone Dashboard does not replace the AppHost project's hosting dependencies. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue in the [Aspire repository](https://github.com/microsoft/aspire). ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-120006](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-120006) ### Acknowledgements - samthewhitehat ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-114155 - .NET Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in the .NET SDK's dotnet-watch component. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected SDK installations. A local attacker who can replace or modify a temporary solution file used by dotnet-watch can alter a subsequent build. The fix stores generated solution files in a private temporary directory and keeps each file open with read-only sharing while the build uses it. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/57040 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-367 - **MSRC severity:** Important - **Impact:** Elevation of Privilege ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS. - **Architectures:** Linux: Arm, Arm64, x64; macOS: Arm64, x64 Windows is outside this advisory's affected scope when its temporary directory is private to the current user, as assumed by the implementation. Shared or insecurely configured Windows temporary directories are not covered by that assumption. ## Affected Packages The .NET SDK includes dotnet-watch and the Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch assembly. Each SDK feature band is a separate servicing line. Update an affected 10.0.3xx installation to the fixed 10.0.4xx SDK listed below. ### .NET SDK 10.0.3xx Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [.NET SDK (dotnet-watch) 10.0.3xx](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.303 | 10.0.404 ### .NET SDK 10.0.4xx Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [.NET SDK (dotnet-watch) 10.0.4xx](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0) | >= 10.0.400, <= 10.0.403 | 10.0.404 ### .NET SDK 11.0.1xx Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [.NET SDK (dotnet-watch) 11.0.1xx](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0) | >= 11.0.100-preview.3.26207.106, <= 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148 | 11.0.100 ### Separately restored Aspire watch tool Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.303 | 10.0.404 [Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire) | >= 10.0.400, <= 10.0.403 | 10.0.404 [Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire) | >= 11.0.100-preview.3.26207.106, <= 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148 | 11.0.100 This tool has its own copy of the watch implementation. Updating the SDK does not necessarily replace a separately restored tool. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Run `dotnet --version` from the directory where you run dotnet-watch to identify the selected SDK. Use `dotnet --info` and `dotnet --list-sdks` to check its installation path, OS, architecture, and other installed SDKs. Check the nearest applicable `global.json`, including its `version` and `rollForward` settings: installing a newer SDK does not necessarily change the SDK selected for a pinned project. See [.NET SDK selection](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/versions/selection). Review use of dotnet-watch against the affected intervals above. Membership in a listed feature band alone does not establish that a specific SDK version is vulnerable. For Aspire or other tooling that separately restores Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire, check the actual restored package version separately from the selected SDK. ### How do I fix the issue? The fixed SDK versions are 10.0.404 and 11.0.100, as applicable. Update each affected SDK installation and restart dotnet-watch. For SDKs installed through Visual Studio, update Visual Studio to a release that includes a fixed SDK. Updating only an application runtime does not replace SDK-bundled tools. Ensure that `global.json` and its SDK roll-forward policy select a fixed SDK, then rerun `dotnet --version` in the working directory to verify the selection. The SDK-bundled watch tool is installed beneath that selected SDK's `DotnetTools/dotnet-watch` directory. If Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire is restored separately, update its package reference or the consuming tool's version configuration to 10.0.404 or 11.0.100, as applicable, restore the tool, and restart the consuming process. An SDK update alone does not update that restored copy. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-114155](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-114155) ### Acknowledgements - [Ky0toFu](https://x.com/ky0tofu) ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

Each advisory below remains the authoritative source for its affected versions and remediation. The fixes and required actions differ by CVE; a runtime or SDK update does not replace every standalone package or repair every application. **Feedback:** [Use the shared .NET Runtime feedback thread](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/137280). Please include the CVE number in your question. **Announcement:** [November 2026 .NET Runtime security updates](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/498). Original CVE-2026-118746 advisory details (preserved) ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Unix Negotiate authentication can accept a request when required channel-binding information is missing. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/137280 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 6.8 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-636 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** Arm, Arm64, x64 ## Affected Packages The tables list affected .NET 11 runtime package versions and fixed versions. The issue occurs during server-side Negotiate authentication with `PolicyEnforcement.Always` when the client omits the channel-binding token. ### .NET 11.0 - Linux runtime packages Package | Affected [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-x64) | > 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103, < 11.0.0 | 11.0.0 The six Linux runtime packages at version 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103 reject `PolicyEnforcement.Always` before authentication and are not affected. ### .NET 11.0 - macOS runtime packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.osx-arm64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103 | 11.0.0 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.osx-x64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103 | 11.0.0 The macOS runtime packages at versions 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103, 11.0.0-rc.1.26425.128, 11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105, and 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148 reject `PolicyEnforcement.Always` before authentication and are not affected. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Applications using server-side Negotiate authentication with `PolicyEnforcement.Always` are affected when their runtime package version is in the platform-specific ranges above. On Linux, this includes .NET 11 previews 1 through 6 and release candidates 1 through 3. On macOS, this includes .NET 11 previews 1 through 6. Preview 7 is not affected on either platform, and macOS release candidates 1 through 3 are not affected. Self-contained applications include their own runtime; updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace it. ### How do I fix the issue? For affected Linux and macOS .NET 11 prereleases, install .NET 11.0.0 or update each independently referenced runtime package to 11.0.0. Restart applications. Rebuild and redeploy self-contained applications; updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace their embedded runtime. An SDK update alone does not update an application's standalone package references. On macOS, `PolicyEnforcement.Always` remains unsupported and throws `PlatformNotSupportedException`. The update prevents authentication from proceeding without the required protection; it does not add Extended Protection support on macOS. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Issues.Body:
> This issue is a locked mirror of https://github.com/dotnet/core/discussions/10711. See that thread for discussion.

We are pleased to announce the general availability of .NET 11.

Read about the final release in the [.NET Blog announcement](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/announcing-dotnet-11/).

This release includes C# 15, faster developer tools, runtime and library improvements, and new capabilities for web, mobile, desktop, and AI apps. Explore the full release notes below.

## 🛠️ SDK

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/sdk.md)

## 📱 .NET MAUI

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/dotnetmaui.md)

## 🎁 Entity Framework Core

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/efcore.md)

## 📚 Libraries

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/libraries.md)

## ⏱️ Runtime

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/runtime.md)

## C# 15

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/csharp.md)

## F# 11

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/fsharp.md)

## 🌐 ASP.NET Core & Blazor

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/aspnetcore.md)

## 🖥️ Windows Forms

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/winforms.md)

## 🖥️ Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF)

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/wpf.md)

## 🚀 Get started

To get started with .NET 11, [install the .NET 11 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0).

If you're on Windows using Visual Studio, use an up-to-date [Visual Studio 2026](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/vs/) installation that supports .NET 11.

You can also use Visual Studio Code and the [C# Dev Kit](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-dotnettools.csdevkit) extension with .NET 11.

Before upgrading an existing application, review the [breaking changes in .NET 11](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/compatibility/11), update your target frameworks and dependencies, and run your tests.

Celebrate the release of .NET 11 at [.NET Conf 2026](https://dot.net/conf), November 10-13.

## 🔔 Stay up-to-date with .NET 11

You can stay up-to-date with all the features of .NET 11 with:

* [What's new in .NET 11](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/whats-new/dotnet-11/overview)
* [What's new in C# 15](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/csharp/whats-new/csharp-15)
* [What's new in F# 11](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/fsharp/whats-new/fsharp-11)
* [What's new in .NET MAUI](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/maui/whats-new/dotnet-11?view=net-maui-11.0)
* [What's new in ASP.NET Core](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/release-notes/aspnetcore-11)
* [What's new in Aspire](https://aspire.dev/whats-new/)
* [What's new in Entity Framework Core](https://learn.microsoft.com/ef/core/what-is-new/ef-core-11.0/whatsnew)
* [What's new in Windows Forms](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/desktop/winforms/whats-new/net110)
* [What's new in WPF](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/desktop/wpf/whats-new/net110)
* [Breaking changes in .NET 11](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/compatibility/11)
* [.NET 11 releases](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/README.md)

Be sure to subscribe to the GitHub Discussions [RSS news feed](https://github.com/dotnet/core/discussions/categories/news.atom) for all release announcements.
